name: Trepanning
desc: Drilling or scraping a hole in the skull, the oldest known surgical procedure, with many survivors showing healed bone.

name: Dentistry
desc: Treating teeth, first attested by bow-drilled molars at Neolithic Mehrgarh.

name: Herbal medicine
desc: Systematic use of plants as remedies, recorded on Sumerian tablets and the basis of most early pharmacology.

name: Opium
desc: Dried poppy latex used since antiquity to relieve pain and induce sleep.

name: Surgical suture
desc: Stitching wounds closed with thread, practiced in ancient Egypt and India.

name: Cauterization
desc: Burning tissue with hot metal to stop bleeding and close wounds.

name: Edwin Smith Papyrus
desc: An Egyptian surgical treatise describing wounds and fractures with rational diagnosis and treatment.

name: Ebers Papyrus
desc: An Egyptian medical text listing hundreds of remedies and prescriptions.

name: Prosthesis
desc: Artificial body parts, from the wooden Cairo toe of ancient Egypt onward.

name: Dentures
desc: Removable replacement teeth, first made by the Etruscans with gold bands.

name: Ayurveda
desc: The classical Indian medical system codified in the Charaka and Sushruta texts.

name: Sushruta Samhita
desc: An Indian surgical text describing over 300 procedures, including nasal reconstruction.

name: Cataract surgery
desc: Removing or displacing a clouded lens to restore sight, first by couching.

name: Hippocratic medicine
desc: Greek texts treating disease as natural rather than divine and stressing observation and prognosis.

name: Huangdi Neijing
desc: The foundational text of traditional Chinese medicine.

name: De materia medica
desc: Dioscorides' pharmacopoeia of about 600 plants, the standard drug reference for 1,500 years.

name: Bimaristan
desc: Hospitals of the medieval Islamic world, with wards, pharmacies and medical teaching.

name: Canon of Medicine
desc: Avicenna's medical encyclopedia, a standard text in Europe and the Islamic world for centuries.

name: Eyeglasses
desc: Lenses in frames worn to correct vision, first made in Italy.

name: Quarantine
desc: Isolating arrivals to stop the spread of plague, first decreed in Ragusa.

name: Pharmacopoeia
desc: An official book standardizing drug preparations, beginning with the Florence Ricettario.

name: Variolation
desc: Deliberate infection with mild smallpox material to confer immunity, practiced in China, India and Africa.

name: De humani corporis fabrica
desc: Vesalius' illustrated anatomy based on dissection, founding modern anatomy.

name: Surgical ligature
desc: Tying off blood vessels during amputation, popularized by Ambroise Pare in place of cautery.

name: Wheelchair
desc: A chair on wheels for people unable to walk, built for Philip II of Spain.

name: Obstetric forceps
desc: Hinged blades for assisting difficult births, invented by the Chamberlen family.

name: Circulation of the blood
desc: William Harvey's proof that the heart pumps blood around a closed circuit.

name: Clinical trial
desc: Comparing treatments on groups of patients, as in James Lind's scurvy trial.

name: Digitalis
desc: Withering's foxglove extract for dropsy; its glycoside digoxin still treats heart failure.

name: Ambulance
desc: Vehicles carrying the sick and wounded to care, first used for emergency transport by Spanish forces in 1487 and later motorized.

name: Morphine
desc: The first alkaloid isolated from a plant, giving a pure, dosable painkiller.

name: Endoscopy
desc: Viewing inside body cavities through an instrument, begun with Bozzini's Lichtleiter.

name: Stethoscope
desc: Laennec's tube for listening to the heart and lungs, founding auscultation.

name: Blood transfusion
desc: Transferring blood between people, first done human to human by James Blundell.

name: Dental braces
desc: Wire appliances that gradually straighten teeth, the core of orthodontics.

name: Quinine
desc: The antimalarial alkaloid isolated from cinchona bark, the first effective malaria drug.

name: Dental amalgam
desc: A mercury alloy filling that made durable dental restorations cheap.

name: Intravenous therapy
desc: Infusing fluids into a vein, first used by Thomas Latta to treat cholera.

name: Salicylic acid
desc: The fever and pain reducer derived from willow bark, precursor of aspirin.

name: Hand washing
desc: Semmelweis showed that washing hands in chlorine solution cut childbed fever deaths.

name: Ophthalmoscope
desc: Helmholtz's instrument for viewing the retina in the living eye.

name: Hypodermic syringe
desc: A hollow needle and syringe for injecting drugs under the skin.

name: Epidemiological mapping
desc: John Snow traced cholera to a water pump, founding modern epidemiology.

name: Antiseptic surgery
desc: Lister's use of carbolic acid to kill germs in wounds, sharply cutting surgical deaths.

name: Clinical thermometer
desc: Allbutt's short, fast-reading mercury thermometer that made fever measurement routine.

name: Attenuated vaccine
desc: Pasteur's weakened chicken cholera culture, the first laboratory-made live vaccine.

name: Autoclave
desc: A pressurized steam chamber that sterilizes instruments and dressings.

name: Cystoscope
desc: Nitze's illuminated scope for the bladder, the first practical endoscope.

name: Tracheal intubation
desc: Passing a tube into the windpipe to secure the airway during anesthesia.

name: Sphygmomanometer
desc: A cuff and gauge for measuring blood pressure, refined by Riva-Rocci in 1896.

name: Local anesthesia
desc: Koller's use of cocaine to numb the eye, allowing surgery on a conscious patient.

name: Rabies vaccine
desc: Pasteur's vaccine from dried infected spinal cord, the first against a human virus disease.

name: Contact lens
desc: A lens worn on the eye's surface, first made of blown glass.

name: Surgical gloves
desc: Thin rubber gloves worn in surgery, introduced by William Halsted.

name: Aseptic technique
desc: Keeping germs out of the operating field through sterilized instruments, gowns and drapes.

name: Diphtheria antitoxin
desc: Behring and Kitasato's serum therapy, neutralizing a bacterial toxin with animal antibodies.

name: Paracetamol
desc: A pain and fever reliever, also called acetaminophen, first used clinically in 1893.

name: Internal fixation
desc: Repairing fractures with metal plates and screws, pioneered by Arbuthnot Lane.

name: Inactivated vaccine
desc: Vaccines from killed microbes, beginning with typhoid and cholera vaccines in 1896.

name: Radiation therapy
desc: Using ionizing radiation to destroy tumors, tried within a year of X-rays' discovery.

name: Fluoroscopy
desc: Real-time X-ray imaging on a fluorescent screen.

name: Aspirin
desc: Acetylsalicylic acid, synthesized at Bayer, a pain reliever later used to prevent heart attacks.

name: Spinal anaesthesia
desc: Injecting anesthetic into the spinal fluid to numb the lower body.

name: Electric hearing aid
desc: An amplifying device for the hard of hearing, first built from telephone parts.

name: ABO blood typing
desc: Landsteiner's discovery of blood groups, making transfusion safe.

name: Adrenaline
desc: The first hormone isolated, used for shock, asthma and severe allergy.

name: Vascular anastomosis
desc: Carrel's technique for suturing blood vessels end to end, enabling transplants.

name: Electrocardiography
desc: Recording the heart's electrical activity, made practical by Einthoven's string galvanometer.

name: Cell culture
desc: Growing living cells outside the body, essential for virus vaccines and biology.

name: Intrauterine device
desc: A small device placed in the uterus for long-acting contraception.

name: Salvarsan
desc: Ehrlich's arsenical cure for syphilis, the first modern synthetic chemotherapeutic drug.

name: Laparoscopy
desc: Examining the abdomen through a small incision with a scope, first done by Jacobaeus.

name: Radioactive tracer
desc: Hevesy's use of radioisotopes to follow substances through living systems.

name: Mammography
desc: X-ray imaging of the breast to detect cancer early.

name: Arthroscopy
desc: Looking inside joints through a small scope, now a routine way to repair them.

name: Phage therapy
desc: Treating bacterial infections with viruses that kill bacteria, revived against resistant strains.

name: Microsurgery
desc: Surgery under an operating microscope, used for ear, eye and vessel repair.

name: BCG vaccine
desc: An attenuated bovine bacillus vaccine against tuberculosis.

name: Insulin therapy
desc: Banting and Best's pancreatic extract that turned type 1 diabetes from fatal to manageable.

name: Toxoid vaccine
desc: Vaccines made from inactivated bacterial toxins, used against diphtheria and tetanus.

name: Electroencephalography
desc: Hans Berger's recording of the brain's electrical rhythms from the scalp.

name: Angiography
desc: X-ray imaging of blood vessels using injected contrast, introduced by Egas Moniz.

name: Iron lung
desc: A negative-pressure ventilator that kept paralyzed polio patients breathing.

name: Cardiac catheterization
desc: Threading a catheter into the heart, first done by Forssmann on himself.

name: Chloroquine
desc: A synthetic antimalarial that replaced quinine for decades.

name: Sulfonamides
desc: Prontosil and its successors, the first broadly effective antibacterial drugs.

name: Heparin
desc: An injectable anticoagulant that made dialysis and heart surgery possible.

name: Blood bank
desc: Storing donated, typed and anticoagulated blood for later transfusion.

name: Yellow fever vaccine
desc: Theiler's 17D live vaccine, among the most effective ever made.

name: Chemotherapy
desc: Treating cancer with cytotoxic drugs, starting with nitrogen mustard for lymphoma.

name: Medical ultrasound
desc: Imaging the body with reflected sound, applied to obstetrics by Ian Donald in 1958.

name: Antihistamines
desc: Drugs blocking histamine to treat allergy, the first being phenbenzamine.

name: Hemodialysis
desc: Kolff's artificial kidney, filtering blood through a membrane outside the body.

name: Streptomycin
desc: An antibiotic from soil bacteria, the first effective against tuberculosis.

name: Influenza vaccine
desc: Egg-grown inactivated flu vaccines, now updated yearly for circulating strains.

name: Defibrillator
desc: Delivering an electric shock to restore a normal heartbeat, first done in surgery by Claude Beck.

name: Methotrexate
desc: A folic acid antagonist chemotherapy drug first made in 1947; it gave the first cures of a metastatic cancer in 1956.

name: Stereotactic surgery
desc: Guiding instruments to precise brain targets using a 3D coordinate frame.

name: Randomized controlled trial
desc: Assigning treatments at random, first done in the MRC streptomycin trial.

name: Tetracyclines
desc: A broad-spectrum antibiotic family from Streptomyces, starting with chlortetracycline.

name: Cephalosporins
desc: Beta-lactam antibiotics from a Sardinian mold, now in five generations.

name: Cortisone
desc: The first corticosteroid used as a drug, dramatically relieving rheumatoid arthritis.

name: DPT vaccine
desc: A combined vaccine against diphtheria, pertussis and tetanus.

name: Myoelectric prosthesis
desc: An artificial limb driven by electrical signals from the wearer's muscles.

name: Lithium therapy
desc: Cade's discovery that lithium salts stabilize bipolar disorder, the first mood stabilizer.

name: Intraocular lens
desc: Ridley's plastic lens implanted after cataract removal to restore focus.

name: Cobalt therapy
desc: Teletherapy with reactor-made cobalt-60, delivering deep, high-energy radiation to tumors.

name: Norethisterone
desc: An orally active synthetic progestin, the key ingredient of the first birth control pills.

name: Artificial heart valve
desc: A mechanical valve implant, first a caged ball placed by Hufnagel.

name: Isoniazid
desc: A cheap oral tuberculosis drug that, combined with others, made TB curable.

name: Chlorpromazine
desc: The first antipsychotic, which emptied asylums and began modern psychopharmacology.

name: Positive-pressure ventilation
desc: Pushing air into the lungs through a tube, adopted during the Copenhagen polio epidemic.

name: Osseointegration
desc: Branemark's finding that bone bonds directly to titanium, basis of implants.

name: Heart-lung machine
desc: A pump-oxygenator taking over circulation, enabling Gibbon's first open-heart operation.

name: Echocardiography
desc: Ultrasound imaging of the beating heart and its valves.

name: Intensive care unit
desc: A ward for continuous monitoring and life support, first set up in Copenhagen.

name: Medical linear accelerator
desc: Megavoltage X-ray machines for cancer treatment, built on wartime microwave tubes.

name: Kidney transplantation
desc: Murray's transplant between identical twins, the first successful organ transplant.

name: Warfarin
desc: An oral anticoagulant derived from spoiled sweet clover, used for decades against clots.

name: Polio vaccine
desc: Salk's inactivated (1955) and Sabin's oral (1961) vaccines that nearly eradicated polio.

name: Fiber-optic endoscope
desc: A flexible scope using glass fiber bundles, letting doctors see inside the gut.

name: Gamma camera
desc: Anger's camera imaging gamma rays from injected tracers, founding nuclear medicine imaging.

name: Metformin
desc: A synthetic biguanide drug developed from research on French lilac (goat's rue); first-line medication for type 2 diabetes.

name: Tricyclic antidepressants
desc: Imipramine and relatives, the first widely used antidepressants.

name: Cardiac pacemaker
desc: An electronic device stimulating the heart, first fully implanted in Sweden in 1958.

name: Thiazide diuretics
desc: Oral diuretics that became the first well-tolerated treatment for high blood pressure.

name: HLA tissue typing
desc: Matching tissue antigens between donor and recipient to reduce rejection.

name: Radioimmunoassay
desc: Yalow and Berson's method of measuring tiny amounts of hormones with labeled antibodies.

name: Azathioprine
desc: An immunosuppressant that let kidney transplants succeed between unrelated people.

name: Telemedicine
desc: Delivering care at a distance, starting with closed-circuit TV psychiatry links.

name: Oral contraceptive pill
desc: A daily hormonal pill preventing ovulation, approved in the US in 1960.

name: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation
desc: Closed-chest compression with rescue breathing to keep circulation going in cardiac arrest.

name: Benzodiazepines
desc: Anxiety and sleep drugs such as diazepam, safer in overdose than barbiturates.

name: Coronary bypass surgery
desc: Grafting vessels around blocked coronary arteries.

name: Cochlear implant
desc: An implant stimulating the auditory nerve electrically, restoring hearing to the deaf.

name: Ibuprofen
desc: A nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory painkiller developed by Boots.

name: Hip replacement
desc: Charnley's low-friction joint of metal and plastic, the model for joint replacement.

name: Beta blockers
desc: Black's drugs blocking adrenaline receptors, treating angina, hypertension and arrhythmia.

name: Quinolones
desc: Synthetic antibiotics found as a by-product of chloroquine synthesis.

name: Measles vaccine
desc: Enders' live attenuated vaccine, preventing millions of child deaths each decade.

name: SPECT
desc: Tomographic imaging of gamma-emitting tracers, showing blood flow and function.

name: Laser surgery
desc: Cutting or sealing tissue with laser light, first used on the retina.

name: Dental implant
desc: A titanium post fused to the jawbone to anchor a replacement tooth.

name: Liposome
desc: Lipid bilayer vesicles described by Bangham, later used to carry drugs.

name: Ventricular assist device
desc: A mechanical pump supporting a failing heart, first implanted by DeBakey.

name: Heart transplantation
desc: Barnard's 1967 transplant of a human heart, routine once ciclosporin arrived.

name: Liver transplantation
desc: Replacing a failed liver, first with lasting success by Thomas Starzl.

name: Phacoemulsification
desc: Kelman's method of breaking up a cataract with ultrasound through a tiny incision.

name: Bone marrow transplant
desc: Transplanting blood-forming stem cells to treat leukemia and immune disorders.

name: Gamma Knife
desc: Leksell's array of cobalt beams converging on a brain target without opening the skull.

name: Oral rehydration therapy
desc: A drink of salts and sugar that treats cholera and diarrhea, saving millions of children.

name: Artificial heart
desc: A mechanical pump replacing the heart, first implanted in 1969 and as the Jarvik-7 in 1982.

name: CT scan
desc: Hounsfield's computed tomography, reconstructing cross-sections from many X-ray views.

name: ELISA
desc: An antibody test using enzyme color changes instead of radioactivity.

name: MMR vaccine
desc: A combined live vaccine against measles, mumps and rubella.

name: Glucose meter
desc: A portable meter reading blood sugar from a fingerstick drop.

name: Artemisinin
desc: Tu Youyou's antimalarial from sweet wormwood, found by searching classical Chinese texts.

name: Electronic health record
desc: Computerized patient records, now the backbone of hospital information systems.

name: Pulse oximetry
desc: Aoyagi's clip-on sensor measuring blood oxygen by light absorption.

name: Hybridoma technology
desc: Kohler and Milstein's fused cells that produce one pure monoclonal antibody.

name: PET scan
desc: Imaging metabolism by detecting positron-emitting tracers such as FDG.

name: Insulin pump
desc: A wearable pump giving continuous, programmable insulin doses.

name: MRI
desc: Imaging soft tissue with nuclear magnetic resonance, without ionizing radiation.

name: Coronary angioplasty
desc: Gruentzig's balloon opening of a narrowed coronary artery through a catheter.

name: Aciclovir
desc: The first selective antiviral drug, a nucleoside analog against herpes viruses.

name: In vitro fertilisation
desc: Fertilizing an egg in the lab, producing Louise Brown, the first IVF baby.

name: Automated external defibrillator
desc: A portable defibrillator that analyzes rhythm and guides untrained rescuers.

name: Smallpox eradication
desc: The WHO campaign that ended smallpox, the first human disease eradicated.

name: Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator
desc: Mirowski's implant that detects and shocks deadly heart rhythms.

name: ACE inhibitors
desc: Captopril and successors, drugs for hypertension and heart failure modeled on snake venom peptides.

name: Hepatitis B vaccine
desc: The first vaccine preventing a cancer (liver), later made by recombinant yeast.

name: Ciclosporin
desc: A fungal immunosuppressant that made heart, liver and lung transplants routine.

name: Lung transplantation
desc: Replacing diseased lungs, first with lasting success in Toronto.

name: Digital radiography
desc: Capturing X-ray images electronically instead of on film.

name: HIV test
desc: Antibody screening for HIV, protecting the blood supply from 1985.

name: Robot-assisted surgery
desc: Surgery with robotic instruments, from the PUMA biopsy robot onward.

name: Monoclonal antibody therapy
desc: Drugs made of antibodies targeting one molecule, first muromonab for transplant rejection.

name: Coronary stent
desc: A mesh tube keeping a reopened artery open after angioplasty.

name: Zidovudine
desc: AZT, the first approved drug against HIV.

name: SSRIs
desc: Antidepressants such as fluoxetine with fewer side effects than tricyclics.

name: Statins
desc: Cholesterol-lowering drugs blocking HMG-CoA reductase, cutting heart attacks and strokes.

name: Photorefractive keratectomy
desc: Reshaping the cornea with an excimer laser to correct vision.

name: Deep brain stimulation
desc: Implanted electrodes delivering pulses to brain targets to treat Parkinson's tremor.

name: Lateral flow test
desc: A paper strip giving a quick visual antigen or antibody result, as in home pregnancy tests.

name: Gene therapy
desc: Treating disease by delivering genes into cells, first tried for ADA immunodeficiency.

name: LASIK
desc: Laser reshaping of the cornea under a surgical flap, the common vision correction surgery.

name: Preimplantation genetic diagnosis
desc: Testing IVF embryos for genetic disease before transfer.

name: Evidence-based medicine
desc: Basing clinical decisions on systematic review of trial evidence.

name: Functional MRI
desc: MRI that maps brain activity through changes in blood oxygen.

name: IMRT
desc: Computer-shaped radiation beams that conform dose closely to a tumor.

name: HIV protease inhibitors
desc: Drugs such as saquinavir blocking HIV's protease, key to combination therapy.

name: Combination antiretroviral therapy
desc: Three-drug regimens that turned HIV from fatal to a chronic, manageable condition.

name: Clear aligners
desc: Computer-designed transparent plastic trays that straighten teeth in steps.

name: Trastuzumab
desc: A humanized antibody against HER2 breast cancer, a model of targeted therapy.

name: Antisense therapy
desc: Short synthetic nucleic acids that block a target RNA, first approved as fomivirsen.

name: Hand transplantation
desc: Transplanting a donor hand, the first composite tissue transplant.

name: Brain-computer interface
desc: Implants or sensors letting paralyzed people control computers by thought.

name: Continuous glucose monitor
desc: A skin sensor tracking blood sugar every few minutes.

name: Tissue engineering
desc: Growing replacement tissue on scaffolds, first used for lab-grown bladders.

name: Da Vinci Surgical System
desc: The surgeon-controlled robot that made robotic laparoscopy widespread.

name: Imatinib
desc: A kinase inhibitor against chronic myeloid leukemia, the landmark of targeted cancer drugs.

name: Capsule endoscopy
desc: A swallowed camera pill imaging the small intestine.

name: Remote surgery
desc: Operating on a patient from far away, as in the transatlantic Lindbergh operation.

name: Transcatheter valve replacement
desc: Implanting a new aortic valve through a catheter instead of open-heart surgery.

name: GLP-1 receptor agonists
desc: Gut-hormone mimics such as exenatide and semaglutide that treat diabetes and obesity.

name: HPV vaccine
desc: A virus-like particle vaccine preventing cervical and other cancers.

name: Checkpoint inhibitors
desc: Antibodies releasing immune brakes such as CTLA-4 and PD-1 so T cells attack cancer.

name: HIV PrEP
desc: Taking antiretrovirals in advance to prevent HIV infection.

name: Retinal implant
desc: An electrode array stimulating the retina to give partial sight to the blind.

name: Sofosbuvir
desc: A nucleotide antiviral that made hepatitis C curable in weeks.

name: Artificial pancreas
desc: A closed loop of glucose sensor, algorithm and pump that doses insulin automatically.

name: CAR T-cell therapy
desc: Patients' T cells engineered with an antibody-based receptor to kill cancer.

name: Voretigene neparvovec
desc: An AAV gene therapy for inherited blindness, the first in vivo gene therapy approved in the US.

name: Patisiran
desc: The first RNA interference drug, delivered in lipid nanoparticles.

name: Medical AI
desc: Algorithms reading scans and images, first cleared for autonomous diabetic retinopathy diagnosis.

name: Viral vector vaccine
desc: Vaccines using a harmless virus to deliver an antigen gene, first licensed against Ebola.

name: mRNA vaccine
desc: Vaccines delivering lipid-wrapped messenger RNA, first deployed at scale against COVID-19.

name: Malaria vaccine
desc: RTS,S and R21, the first vaccines against a parasitic disease.

name: Xenotransplantation
desc: Transplanting gene-edited pig organs into humans, first a heart in 2022.

name: CRISPR gene therapy
desc: Casgevy, the first approved CRISPR-edited therapy, for sickle cell disease.
